quarterly_data.quarter: Amtech Systems LD Micro main event 2026 (10-20-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Executive Chairman Bob Daigle on TrueFlat reflow capacity: about 18 months ago Amtech was producing about four of these systems per week in its Shanghai factory; last quarter it produced about 10-12 a week, 'so about threefold number of units', and lead times are still six weeks (two weeks build, two weeks test). Amtech is 'semi-fabless': Shanghai assembles, tests and ships, and a contractor in the Malaysia-Singapore area serves the U.S. market because of tariffs. The restructuring took Amtech from seven factories to four facilities, only one of which still builds equipment.
quarterly_data.figure: about 10-12 systems a week last quarter (about four a week 18 months ago); lead time six weeks

quarterly_data.quarter: Amtech Systems LD Micro main event 2026 (10-20-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Executive Chairman Bob Daigle on position and strategy: Amtech's high-temperature TrueFlat furnaces (patented vacuum hold-down that keeps substrates flat) melt the ball grid arrays that assemble GPU packages on the substrate - 'We own this space. The majority of GPUs, TPUs, use our equipment'; customers are the OSATs, the memory makers and the processor makers (not named). Annualized revenue is about $90 million, 80% Thermal Processing Solutions and about 20% Semiconductor Fabrication Solutions; with industry tailwinds alone he thinks the company 'could be $150' million, and its TAM supports 20%, 30% growth. Amtech takes part in one of eight operations used to make these packages; customers are asking it to move into other steps now served by low-throughput batch tools, where he thinks it might get three, four times its current price versus the 10 times customers pay others, and where TAM and margins could be higher.
quarterly_data.figure: annualized revenue about $90 million (80% TPS); one of eight package operations

quarterly_data.quarter: Amtech Systems LD Micro main event 2026 (10-20-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Executive Chairman Bob Daigle on orders: the segment's book-to-bill was just about 1.4 to 1 last quarter and 1.2 the prior quarter; large customers worried about the supply chain supporting growth ('the Nvidias of the world') are pushing everyone to order ahead, so bookings last quarter went out a quarter or two - backlog this segment historically has not had, after typically booking and shipping in the same quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: book-to-bill about 1.4 to 1 last quarter, 1.2 the prior quarter

quarterly_data.quarter: Amtech Systems LD Micro main event 2026 (10-20-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Executive Chairman Bob Daigle on technology transitions: Amtech does not play in thermal compression bonding or hybrid bonding for high bandwidth memory and probably would not; he sees co-packaged optics ('It's just starting') and panel-level packaging as tailwinds where Amtech has process-of-record experience and where higher yield demands favor its equipment, as CPUs, automotive, DoD and some medical applications did before AI. On U.S. onshoring, packaging is coming (Amkor has announced) but is 'still probably 18, 24 months out' and will take longer than wafer fabs because of skills.

quarterly_data.quarter: Amtech Systems LD Micro main event 2026 (10-20-2026)
quarterly_data.signal: Executive Chairman Bob Daigle: Amtech now has $83 million in cash and no debt. It may make small acquisitions, more likely of privately held, small companies, of enabling technology (motor drives, vacuum systems, components) that would speed its path to cleaner Class 1,000 and Class 100 process steps; he does not expect a dilutive deal or a large target.
